a1.say: Let's solve Same Shape Strings, using the Two Hash Maps approach.

a1.cap: Two strings have the same shape (they are isomorphic) if you can replace each character of s with another character, consistently and one-to-one, to obtain t. Return true if s and t have the same shape.

lines: Two strings have the same shape (they are isomorphic) if you can replace each character of s with another character, consistently and one-to-one, to obtain t. Return true if s and t have the same shape.

a1.cap: For example, with s = "egg", t = "add", the answer is true. e→a, g→d.
a1.say: For example, with s equals "egg", t equals "add", the answer is true. e to a, g to d.

a1.cap: Keep a map from s letters to t letters and another map back. Walk both strings together; if either map already holds a different partner, the shapes differ.
Let's walk through it with s = "paper", t = "title".
a1.say: Let's walk through it with s equals "paper", t equals "title".

a1.cap: Time complexity is O(n) and extra space is O(1).
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n and extra space is O of one.

a1.cap: That's the Two Hash Maps approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
